canonical.title: Making A Large Island
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/5. MST Problems/07. Making Large Island.cpp

narrative.title: One Reclamation, Maximum Harbour
narrative.scenario: A port authority may reclaim exactly one water cell into usable dock. Planners want the resulting largest connected dock region: measure every existing region, then test each candidate water cell — reclaiming it merges every distinct region touching its four sides, plus the cell itself. If the harbour is already seamless, the answer is simply its full size.
narrative.inputFormat: An n x n binary matrix grid where 1 is dock and 0 is water.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the size of the largest island after converting at most one 0 to 1.

testCases.explanation: Reclaiming either water cell bridges the two 1-regions into a size-3 harbour.
No water exists to reclaim — the whole grid is already one island.

hintLevels: Level 1: Brute force refills each water cell and re-floods — too slow; measure regions once instead.
Level 2: Union-find every land region, then for each 0 sum the distinct neighbouring root sizes plus one.
Level 3: Deduplicate neighbour roots with a set — two sides of the same island must not be double-counted — and never forget the no-water case.
